horizon_driver: Monthly/quarterly investor redemption windows, internal VaR/risk-limit review cycles, and prime-broker margin calls operate on a days-to-weeks cadence — far shorter than the multi-year horizon of the positions they trade against (e.g. sovereign bond duration).

constraints.source: Large hedge funds' gross US Treasury exposure doubled to $4.0 trillion between 2023 and Sept 2025 ($2.4tn long / $1.6tn short) — Federal Reserve FEDS Notes, 22 Jun 2026 — meaning the basis trade is now large enough that its own unwind moves the market it is arbitraging
constraints.breaks_under: a sharp, unexpected yield move forces margin calls the fund cannot meet without deleveraging; this broke concretely in April-May 2025 when roughly $60bn (20%) of swap-spread positions were unwound in April 2025 and a further $40bn in May 2025 following the 2 Apr 2025 tariff announcement (Federal Reserve Bank of New York speech, 9 May 2025; Fed FEDS Notes, Jun 2026)

stated_vs_revealed.stated: Relative-value and macro hedge funds (including basis-trade funds and multi-strategy pods) describe their arbitrage activity as stabilising — narrowing the cash-futures Treasury basis and improving price discovery and liquidity for the broader market.
stated_vs_revealed.revealed: Following the 2 April 2025 tariff shock, the same funds' deleveraging amplified the stress they claim to dampen: the 10-year Treasury yield surged past 4.5% and 30-year yields rose above 5% between 2-10 April 2025 — the steepest increase since 1981 — as roughly $60bn of swap-spread positions were forcibly unwound in April alone, with a further $40bn in May (New York Fed speech, 9 May 2025; Fed FEDS Notes, Jun 2026; IMF F&D, Mar 2026).
stated_vs_revealed.delta: Large and directly falsifying the 'liquidity provider' self-description under exactly the conditions when liquidity is scarcest — confirming the Cartographer's framing that withdrawal at the moment of maximum need is a feature of the business model, not a failure of it.

stated_vs_revealed.stated: 'Hedge funds' and 'market makers' are often treated as a single class with uniform behaviour under stress.
stated_vs_revealed.revealed: The April 2025 episode split this class visibly in two: balance-sheet-funded market makers (Jane Street, which trades on its own balance sheet rather than external leverage) held positions through the volatility window that forced levered competitors out, while low-latency market maker Citadel Securities saw Treasury volumes and hit-ratios rise sharply (avg daily $70mm per-basis-point sensitivity, 45% hit ratio, gross volume up 75% to $1.4tn) — precisely because it was supplying liquidity levered relative-value funds were withdrawing.
stated_vs_revealed.delta: Moderate structural finding: the internal split is between externally-levered relative-value funds (which withdraw) and balance-sheet-funded/HFT market makers (which often gain share) — worth flagging as a candidate internal-faction split for HF_MACRO even though it is not being split into a separate actor here.

tripwires.if: 10-year Treasury yield moves more than ~75-100bps within a 3-5 day window (comparable to the 2-10 Apr 2025 episode)
tripwires.then: expect forced basis-trade/swap-spread deleveraging on the order of tens of billions per month, which itself further deteriorates liquidity and widens bid-ask spreads — a reflexive, self-reinforcing withdrawal

tripwires.if: hedge-fund gross Treasury exposure continues growing past the $4.0tn (Sept 2025) level
tripwires.then: the system's structural dependence on this class continuing to provide the trade increases, and so does the scale of any future forced unwind

tripwires.if: a levered relative-value fund faces a multi-day margin call it cannot meet
tripwires.then: distinguish it from balance-sheet-funded market makers (Jane Street-type) in the response — the former deleverages and withdraws, the latter often steps in and gains share

what_would_change_my_mind: Fund-level (not aggregate) leverage and redemption-term data for the largest basis-trade managers would let me set a specific yield-move threshold at which forced deleveraging becomes mechanically certain rather than merely likely, as currently inferred from the single April 2025 data point.
